answer.rationale: Under competitive price pressure, promotional_pricing appears immediately attractive but memory_73 explicitly warns it materially reduces 30-day retention despite acquisition lift—directly contradicting the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Referral_incentive (memory_57) works well for established customers but does not address the acute churn risk in price-sensitive SMBs. Simplify_onboarding repeats memory_86/31 gains already captured. The strongest case is activation_messaging (memory_91): confirmed +6% activation and +1% retention lift in a standard experiment frame. Combined with shortened onboarding (memory_86: +3% retention, -2.1 days to value), rapid in-product engagement creates tangible value perception that reduces defection risk without eroding unit economics. This preserves the SMB base while avoiding the retention damage of discounting. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is mismatched to the immediate SMB churn crisis. Activation_messaging is lower-risk, evidence-backed, and defensible as a 1-2 week standard experiment to buy time before deeper pricing decisions. It does not solve price sensitivity but materially improves engagement-driven retention in the cohort most at risk.
